paragraphs.source_en: The first year of Kōji (1555) was an eventful one for Takechiyo. Life’s sorrows and joys assailed him together, allowing him not a moment to catch his breath.

paragraphs.source_en: The painstaking efforts of his retainers finally bore fruit. In March of that year, Yoshimoto personally placed the ceremonial cap upon Takechiyo and conducted his coming-of-age ceremony. Yoshimoto had intended to hold the ceremony when Takechiyo was fifteen, but after repeated entreaties from the Okazaki retainers, he finally brought it forward by a year.

paragraphs.source_en: After coming to Sunpu, Gen’ō-ni had to avoid even the appearance of contact with Takechiyo, lest she arouse suspicion. She was a sorrowful woman cast aside by the world, a woman who lived in the shadows. Though she constantly watched over Takechiyo’s food, clothing, and daily life and secretly lavished boundless affection upon him, she was never permitted to care for him in Yoshimoto’s residence. And to avoid suspicion herself, she never once showed her face at the residence of Sekiguchi Gyōbu-shōyū.

Before long, he received orders to marry.

paragraphs.source_en: For Jirōsaburō, it was not a marriage that pleased him.
